info.name: E-Commerce Inventory & Order Fulfillment - Assignments 1, 2, 3 and 4
info.description:
Complete Postman validation collection for Assignments 1 to 4. Folders 1 to 7 cover authentication, RBAC, dynamic product filtering, orders, coupons, payments, caching, audit logs, the Kafka order flow and Actuator observability. Folders 8 to 10 cover the Phase 4 multi-vendor marketplace: vendor onboarding and per-vendor product ownership, verified-purchase reviews with the rating recalculation engine, and multipart image upload with its rejection cases.

Order matters for the Phase 4 folders. Run folder 1 to obtain tokens, then 8, then 10, then 9 (folder 10 populates the image URL that the review in folder 9 attaches). Running 8 then 9 then 10 also works; the review simply carries no photo.

item.name: 8. Phase 4 - Vendors & Marketplace
item.description:
Assignment Phase 4, Module 2. Run folder 1 first so that adminToken and customerToken are populated.

This folder onboards two vendors, promotes a freshly registered account to ROLE_VENDOR by linking it as the owner of the first vendor, and then proves the ownership boundary: a vendor may create and edit products under its own vendor id and nothing else. The requests are order-dependent - run them top to bottom, or use Run Folder.

item.name: 9. Phase 4 - Reviews & Rating Engine
item.description:
Assignment Phase 4, Module 3. Run folder 8 first: this folder reviews the product created there.

The sequence deliberately walks the whole eligibility gate. A review is attempted while the order is still PENDING (rejected), the order is then paid, and the same review is attempted again (accepted). After the accepted review, the aggregates on both the product and its parent vendor are re-read to confirm the rating engine recalculated them.

request.description: The customer buys the vendor's product. The order starts PENDING, which does not yet qualify as a completed purchase.
Only PAID and SHIPPED orders count as proof of purchase, so a PENDING order is not enough. Expects 403.

exec: pm.test('Unpaid purchase cannot review', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(403); });
pm.test('Message explains the rule', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.include('only review products you have purchased'); });

request.description: Moves the order to PAID, which makes the purchase review-eligible.

The authorized review submission flow. The caller is ROLE_CUSTOMER and now has a PAID order containing this product, so the review is accepted with 201. imageUrl is optional and is filled in by folder 10; leaving it as an unresolved variable simply stores an empty value.

item.name: 10. Phase 4 - Media Upload
item.description:
Assignment Phase 4, Module 4. multipart/form-data image upload with the four rejection cases the acceptance criteria call for: wrong extension, wrong content type, a non-image wearing a .png name, and a file over 2 MB.

File paths are relative to the postman/ folder. In Postman, set the working directory to the repository's postman/ folder (Settings > General > Working directory), or re-select the file with the Select Files button. Run 'python postman/sample-files/generate-samples.py' once to create the sample files, including the oversized one which is not committed.

Run this folder before folder 9 if you want the review to carry a photo, or after it to attach the image to the vendor product.
